title: Djokovic's Season Ends With a Surprise Defeat in Paris
summary: Novak Djokovic's season is over, and it ended with a surprise. The 39-year-old tennis star lost 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 to Rinky Hijikata, a qualifier from Australia ranked 83rd in the world, in the second round of the Paris Masters on Wednesday. The defeat knocked Djokovic out of the race for the ATP Finals in Turin. He likely needed to reach the semi-finals in Paris to qualify, and the draw had seemed to open up for him after two of his rivals lost earlier in the day. Djokovic started well, but Hijikata raised his level late in the second set and through the deciding set, while Djokovic, who looked tired and was struggling physically, made a string of errors. After the match, Djokovic said his plan for the next few weeks is "just rest." "I'm looking forward to it," he added. He praised his opponent, too: "He played really amazing tennis and it was my fault to let the control of the match go." Djokovic, who owns a men's record 24 Grand Slam singles titles, has now failed to qualify for the season-ending event for only the second time in 20 seasons when fit. He reached the Australian Open final and the Wimbledon semi-finals this year, yet he has not reached a quarter-final at any of this year's Masters 1000 events. His last Grand Slam title came at the US Open in 2023. Qualifying for Turin would have given him a shot at a record-extending eighth title at the season-ending championships. Instead, only Americans Taylor Fritz and Tommy Paul remain in the hunt for the final two places, currently held by Frances Tiafoe and Rafael Jodar. Tiafoe lost to France's Quentin Halys, and Alex de Minaur lost to Tomas Martin Etcheverry of Argentina. Zverev and Medvedev, who have both already qualified, were also beaten.
why_it_matters: Even the greatest players can lose to an underdog, and that is what makes sports exciting to watch.
